blocks.text: Scripts are a great way to automate PowerShell scripts for specific device tasks. Zscaler provides predefined scripts to help you get started.
To manage the Scripts page, you must have the following:

blocks.item: The appropriate subscription level. To learn more, see Ranges & Limitations.
The Script Management permission level for Digital Experience (ZDX). To learn more, see Adding ZDX Roles.
If you are running a script, the selected devices must have:
The minimum version compatibility for Zscaler Client Connector and ZDX Module
The supporting OS
If a device is not compatible, then the script does not run on that device. To learn more, see Supported Versions & Feature Compatibility.
If you are uploading a customized script, the script must have a signed certificate. To learn more, see Preparing Custom Script Signing.

blocks.text: From the navigation menu, go to Digital Experience > Devices > Scripts. On the Scripts page, you can:

blocks.item: Add a script.
Click Add Script.
In the Add Script window:
See image.
Script Name: Enter a name for the script.
Description: Enter a description of the script.
Operating System: Select which OS this impacts (Windows).
Upload Script File: Upload a PS1 file to run the script. The maximum script file size when uploading is 512 KB.
Run Script with Elevated Permissions (System Account): Select if you want to run the script on a system account.
Script Parameters (Optional): Add parameters to determine when to run the script.
Parameter Name: Enter a parameter name (e.g., Domain) for the script to evaluate.
Default Value: Enter an example value (e.g., google.com) for the script to evaluate.
Mandatory: Select the checkbox if the parameter is mandatory. By default, this is selected.
See image.
End User Notifications: Show or Hide notifications to the end user. When Show is selected, configure the following to show to the end user prior to running the script:
Message From: Enter the name of the team you want to indicate the message is from.
Header: Enter the name of the header to display.
Question/Message: Enter a question or message.
Accept Button: Enter the text for the Accept button (e.g., Okay).
Decline Button: Enter the text for the Decline button (e.g., Cancel).
Preview: Displays a preview of the configured notification.
See image.
Click Add.
Run a script.
Click the Run icon
In the Start Remediation Job window:
Under Select Script:
Script: Search and select which script you want to run. You can also create a script.
Script Details: If you configured script parameters or an end user notification, then you can modify the script parameters and preview the end user notification.
Script Run Settings: Enter the number of seconds the script can run for.
Under Select Devices, click Add to open the Select Devices drawer.
Criteria: Select Devices, Users, User Groups, Locations, Location Groups, or Departments.
Search: You can search for the name of the selected criteria. Click the Remove icon to reset your search.
Enable Display selected only to filter for your selected criteria.
Click Done to save your selection.
If you cannot select a device, check its version compatibility or OS. To learn more, see Supported Versions & Feature Compatibility.
See image.
Under Job Details:
Wait for devices to be online for a maximum of: Enter the number of minutes or days a script must wait to run on a device.
Schedule Job for later: Enable to select a date for when you want to run the script.
See image.
Click Start.
View the job's progress on the Jobs page.
Edit a script.
Click the Edit icon on the script that you want to modify.
In the Edit Script window, modify any of the fields as needed.
See image.
Click Save Changes.
Delete a script.
Click the Delete icon.
In the Delete Script window, click Delete.

blocks.text: Predefined scripts are useful because they are certified and ready for use script templates. Zscaler recommends testing the script prior to deploying production to devices.
Predefined scripts are found on the Scripts > Templates page (Digital Experience > Devices > Scripts > View Script Templates). For each predefined script, you see:

blocks.item: Name: The name of the predefined script.
Description: The description of the predefined script.
Operating System: The supported OS.
Scripts In Use: Displays the number of scripts currently using the predefined script.
Last Updated: The timestamp of when the predefined script was released.

blocks.text: You can view, search, or import the predefined scripts.
Consider the following when configuring scripts:

blocks.item: The maximum number of scripts you can configure is based on your subscription. To learn more, see Ranges & Limitations.
You can upload to the maximum script file size of 512 KB.
You can import a predefined script only once.

You are unable to run an older version of a predefined remote script if it is revoked. You must delete the previously configured predefined script and import the latest predefined script to continue use.
A script runs for a maximum of 10 minutes.
